title: Telemetry ingest: Backfill snapshot version gate and compatibility bridge
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a safe, auditable way to backfill historical telemetry into the new analytics schema (v5+) without double-counting or breaking downstream consumers. Past migrations caused noisy dashboards and partial reingestion gaps when producers and SDKs advanced at different cadences. This ticket implements a 'snapshot version gate' plus an on-the-fly compatibility bridge that canonicalizes older events into the current canonical schema for reingest and query-time reconciliation.

Goals:
- Provide a reversible, idempotent backfill path for historical event ranges tied to a snapshot marker.
- Ensure no duplication with live traffic (handles overlap windows).
- Preserve provenance metadata (original_schema_version, transform_version, trace_id) so audits can reconstruct what was transformed.
- Minimize cluster impact by batching, rate-limiting, and cost-aware sampling for very large historical ranges.
- Offer operators an emergency abort and partial rollback.

Out-of-scope: full SDK breaking-change mitigation (handled in separate SDK compatibility shims), online schema negotiation handshake improvements (existing work).
acceptance_criteria:
- A backfill run can be initiated against a defined time range with a snapshot tag and completes without producing duplicate events in downstream BigQuery/warehouse views.
- Transformed events include provenance headers: original_schema_version, transform_version.
- Dashboards instrumented for delta detection show <0.5% unexpected drift after canary.
- Operators can pause/abort/trim a running backfill and observe consistent state in the audit log.
- End-to-end smoke tests across SDK->ingest->pipeline validate canonicalization rules for 10 representative event types.
plan:
1) Design: finalize canonical field mapping and repair heuristics for the top 20 event types by volume; define snapshot metadata model.
2) Implementation: build lightweight 'compat-bridge' microservice that accepts legacy envelope, applies deterministic transformations, attaches provenance, and writes to the backfill topic.
3) Ingest integration: extend ingestion pipeline (Kafka/Router layer) to honor snapshot tags and dedupe using (trace_id, snapshot_tag) watermarking.
4) Backfill runner: CLI tool to create snapshot markers, partition historical ranges, and push to compat-bridge with concurrency controls.
5) Canary: run against a 6-hour slice for one customer segment, monitor traffic, and compare to baseline dashboards.
6) Rollout: staged expansion (6h -> 24h -> 7d -> full) with operator checkpoints.

Implementation notes: compat-bridge is stateless, horizontally scalable, written in Go, and exposes a /transform endpoint. Dedupe uses a short-lived Redis LRU for sliding-window duplicate detection and final dedupe is guaranteed by warehouse materialized view keys.
rollout_plan:
- Stage 0 (dev): unit tests + local end-to-end against dev cluster.
- Stage 1 (canary): run 6-hour backfill for internal accounts (canary-telemetry) with strict rate cap (10% of max historical throughput). Monitor cost, error rates, and dashboard drift.
- Stage 2 (pilot): 24-hour run for two paid customers, validate queries and billing.
- Stage 3 (prod): full historical backfill with rollout window and pause checkpoints every 12 hours.
- Post-rollout: 30-day retention of transform logs and a reconciliation job to compare pre/post metrics.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Double-counting where live and backfilled events overlap. Mitigation: snapshot_tag watermarking + canonical trace_id tie-breaker + idempotent write semantics.
- Risk: Compatibility bridge introduces semantic regressions. Mitigation: exhaustive unit tests + golden files for each event type + manual QA signoff.
- Risk: Backfill cost and I/O spikes. Mitigation: rate limiting per shard, progressive backoff, and sampling for low-value event types.
- Risk: Long-running backfills blocked by schema changes. Mitigation: lock snapshot model and require migration PRs to reference active snapshots.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for every transform rule and edge-case fields.
- Integration test: SDK test harness emits legacy events -> compat-bridge -> ingest pipeline -> warehouse; validate schema and counts.
- Canary: endpoint-level tracing to sample 0.1% of transformed events to full-keyed backlogs for manual inspection.
- Load test: synthetic 10x traffic replay to validate rate-limiting and Redis dedupe behavior.
- Reconciliation: daily job comparing md5 checksums of canonicalized event payloads vs expected golden outputs.
